title: A henselian G-ring model retaining a flat group and its split residue fibre
statement: Let $(C,\mathfrak m_C)$ be a commutative henselian local ring [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], put $k=C/\mathfrak m_C$ [def-weil-residue-field], and let $H\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ be an affine flat group scheme of finite presentation [pqf-def-affine-morphism, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. A group scheme is a group object in schemes over its base, and homomorphisms preserve multiplication, identity and inverse. Let $M$ be a finitely generated additive abelian group and suppose an isomorphism $a:D_k(M)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_k$ is given, where $D_R(M)=\operatorname{Spec}R[M]$ has the Hopf operations of [def-sfb-ring-diagonalizable-group] and subscripts denote fibre-product scalar extension [def-pc-fibre-product]. Then there exist a henselian local Noetherian G-ring $(A,\mathfrak m_A)$ [def-weil-pbc-g-ring], a local ring map $u:A\to C$ (meaning $u^{-1}(\mathfrak m_C)=\mathfrak m_A$), a commutative finitely presented $A$-algebra $B$ flat as an $A$-module [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra, def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], a group scheme structure on $H_A=\operatorname{Spec}B$, and a $C$-group isomorphism $b:(H_A)_C\xrightarrow{\sim}H$. Writing $k_A=A/\mathfrak m_A$, there is a $k_A$-group isomorphism $a_A:D_{k_A}(M)\xrightarrow{\sim}(H_A)_{k_A}$ whose scalar extension along the residue embedding $k_A\hookrightarrow k$ followed by $b_k$ is exactly $a$. No injectivity of $u$ and no conditions on fibres of $H_A$ away from its closed point are asserted.

source.place: Agent finite-Hopf-diagram and residue-isomorphism refinement of Tag 0A41 (lemma-henselian-local-limit-G-rings); flatness descent is Tag 04AI (limits.tex, lemma-descend-flat-finite-presentation). The finite Hopf data and specified inverse residue maps are retained by finite-presentation limit descent. This is a model theorem, not a lifting theorem.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-henselian-local-g-ring-colimit] to write $C=\varinjlim_i A_i$ with local transition and cocone maps, each $A_i$ henselian local Noetherian and a G-ring. Write $k_i=A_i/\mathfrak m_i$. The induced maps $k_i\to k_j$ and $k_i\to k$ are injective: their kernels are zero because the original maps contract the maximal ideals exactly. Moreover $k=\varinjlim_i k_i$. Indeed every residue class has a representative in $C$, hence in some $A_i$; two such representatives can be moved to a common stage, and equality of their residues means their difference maps into $\mathfrak m_C$, so is in that stage maximal ideal by locality. Compatible ring maps from the $k_i$ therefore define a unique ring map from $k$, by sending a represented residue class to its stage value. This proves the ring-colimit universal property, not just an equality of sets.

source.place: Tag 0A41, lemma-henselian-local-limit-G-rings; residue-field colimit argument supplied here from locality.

proof.text: Since $H$ is affine over $\operatorname{Spec}C$, write $H=\operatorname{Spec}E$. By [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation], $E$ is finitely presented over $C$; by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion], it is flat over $C$. Apply [lem-kun-fp-algebra-descent] to obtain $i$ and a finitely presented $A_i$-algebra $B_i$ with a specified identification $C\otimes_{A_i}B_i\simeq E$. The affine-spectrum correspondence [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] turn the group operations into algebra maps $\Delta:E\to E\otimes_C E$, $\epsilon:E\to C$, and $s:E\to E$, satisfying the duals of the group diagrams. These statements use the correspondence over the ring $C$, with no field hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 05N9 (lemma-colimit-category-fp-algebras), (1); affine translation: Schemes 01I4 and Morphisms 01TQ, 01U5.

proof.text: For a presentation $B_i=A_i[x]/(f)$, its tensor square and cube have presentations $A_i[x,y]/(f(x),f(y))$ and $A_i[x,y,z]/(f(x),f(y),f(z))$; these follow by the algebra-tensor universal property [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. Their scalar extensions have the same presentations over $C$. Use [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-category-fp-algebras], (2), for the three operation maps, and move to a common stage. Use (3) for the finitely many equations: $(\Delta\otimes1)\Delta=(1\otimes\Delta)\Delta$, $(\epsilon\otimes1)\Delta=1=(1\otimes\epsilon)\Delta$, and $\mu(s\otimes1)\Delta=u\epsilon=\mu(1\otimes s)\Delta$, with the canonical tensor unit and associativity identifications. Each is an equality of maps from the finitely presented $B_i$ into its tensor cube, itself, or its tensor square; the maps agree after extension to $C$. A common later stage enforces all equations. By the affine-spectrum correspondence and affine fibre-product description, their spectra give a group structure on $\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ and the chosen identification with $E$ gives a $C$-group isomorphism $b_i$.

source.place: Tag 05N9, lemma-colimit-category-fp-algebras, (2),(3), applied to the finite group diagrams; tensor presentations written explicitly.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-flat-ring-map] on the tail above the current $i$, with its $B_0=A_i$, $C_0=B_i$ and $\varphi_0$ the structure map. Its limit map is $C\to E$, flat by step 2, and its finite-presentation hypothesis is exactly the chosen presentation of $B_i$. Thus all sufficiently late $A_j\to B_j=A_j\otimes_{A_i}B_i$ are flat. Replace $i$ by such a stage, carrying along the operations and $b_i$ by scalar extension. The equations remain equations after applying a ring map. No flatness of $A_i\to C$ is required.

source.place: Tag 02JO, lemma-flat-finite-presentation-limit-flat, (3); affine algebra form used in Limits Tag 04AI.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-subgroup-algebra-coset-presentation] with $L=0$, every $R[M]$ is finitely presented over $R$; its scalar-extension identification sends $e_m$ to $e_m$. In particular the two $k_i$-algebras $k_i[M]$ and $B_i\otimes_{A_i}k_i$ are finitely presented, the latter by reducing its polynomial presentation. Their extensions to $k=\varinjlim k_j$ are $k[M]$ and $E\otimes_C k$. Translate the specified $a$ and $a^{-1}$ contravariantly using [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-category-fp-algebras], (2), to descend both maps to some $k_j$. Apply (3) to their two inverse equations and to compatibility with coproduct, counit and antipode, for both maps. All targets are finitely presented: their tensor presentations are as in step 3. A common later $j$ makes these equations hold together. The resulting spectra are inverse group maps $a_j:D_{k_j}(M)\simeq (H_j)_{k_j}$. The factorization equations in (2) say precisely that $(b_j)_k\circ(a_j)_k=a$, including this particular supplied isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 05N9, lemma-colimit-category-fp-algebras, (2),(3), now for the residue-field system; finite presentation of the group algebra from the cited subgroup presentation at L=0.

proof.text: Take $A=A_j$, $u=u_j$, $B=B_j$, $H_A=\operatorname{Spec}B_j$, $b=b_j$ and $a_A=a_j$. Step 1 supplies henselianity, Noetherianity, the G-ring property and locality; steps 2--4 supply the finitely presented flat algebra and group structure; step 5 supplies the residue-fibre isomorphism with the required equality. The embedding $k_A\hookrightarrow k$ is the one induced by $u$, already checked in step 1.

source.place: Assembly of the finite-stage choices; Tag 0A41 and the finite-data descent argument above.
